item.title: ASP.NET Core Razor Pages: Populating HTML SELECT Dropdowns with Tag Helpers
item.description:
“ASP.NET Core Razor Pages: Populating HTML SELECT Dropdowns with Tag Helpers”

Generating dynamic <select> elements is a common requirement in web development. In ASP.NET Core Razor Pages or MVC, Tag Helpers offer a clean, HTML-like syntax to achieve this. The core mechanism relies heavily on the asp-items attribute combined with collections that conform to the structure required by the SelectList or SelectListItem.

Method 1: Binding Directly from a Custom ViewModel Collection

A primary approach involves preparing a list of data objects in the Controller or Page Model’s GET action and mapping this to SelectList within the view, utilizing asp-items.

item.title: ASP.NET MVC Razor: Selecting Correct Item in Loop with @Html.DropDownListFor
item.description:
“ASP.NET MVC Razor: Selecting Correct Item in Loop with @Html.DropDownListFor”

How can we reliably ensure the correct option is selected for each element in a collection when using Razor helpers for generating multiple dropdown lists?

Resolving Pre-selection Issues with @Html.DropDownListFor in Collections

Several approaches exist to tackle the challenge of maintaining selection state across dynamically generated dropdown lists bound to a model collection.

Approach 1: Employing an EditorTemplate for Item Types

A robust technique involves leveraging ASP.NET MVC’s convention for partial views—specifically, EditorTemplates. This allows you to define the rendering logic for a complex type once, ensuring consistency and proper model binding.

item.title: Razor CSHTML: Injecting C# Model Data into JavaScript Safely
item.description:
“Razor CSHTML: Injecting C# Model Data into JavaScript Safely”

Embedding server-side C# data from your Razor model directly into client-side JavaScript running within a .cshtml file presents several syntactic and security challenges. Razor is fundamentally an HTML templating engine, not a JavaScript generator, leading to potential compilation errors or Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities if not handled correctly. What are the reliable techniques for transferring data like map coordinates or user details from the C# model to JavaScript variables?
